points.t: Choosing, quantifying or reviewing a topical steroid for eczema, psoriasis or another inflammatory rash.
Glucocorticoid-receptor effects switch off inflammatory genes, constrict vessels and slow turnover; overuse **thins skin**.
**Lowest potency that works, shortest time**; potency by site and age; FTUs; review, then **step down**.
**Tinea incognito**, steroid rosacea / perioral dermatitis, atrophy, **TSW**, adrenal suppression.

cause.lead: Switch off inflammation, at a cost to collagen.
points: Steroid binds the **glucocorticoid receptor** → nucleus.
**Transactivation**: switches on anti-inflammatory genes (annexin-1 → fewer prostaglandins and leukotrienes).
**Transrepression**: blocks **NF-κB and AP-1** → fewer cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α), COX-2.
Also anti-proliferative (useful in psoriasis) and **inhibits fibroblast collagen**: the cause of atrophy.
Potency is measured by the **vasoconstrictor (blanching) assay**.

visuals.caption: Normal skin (left) beside steroid atrophy (right): thin epidermis, sparse collagen and dilated surface vessels, giving shiny, translucent skin that bruises and tears easily.
visuals.alt: Skin sections comparing normal skin and steroid atrophy

features.lead: Match potency to severity, site and age (BNF classes).
points: **Mild** (e.g. hydrocortisone): face, flexures, infants, mild eczema.
**Moderate** (e.g. clobetasone butyrate): moderate eczema on body; short courses face / flexures in adults.
**Potent** (e.g. betamethasone valerate 0.1%, mometasone, hydrocortisone butyrate): severe eczema, body.
**Very potent** (clobetasol): short courses for thick plaques, palms / soles, lichen sclerosus, DLE, scalp.
**Combination products** take their steroid’s potency; occlusion raises effective potency.

visuals.caption: Absorption varies by site (forearm = 1): soles about 0.1, palms 0.8, scalp 3.5, face 7–13, eyelids and genitals up to 40. Thin, flexural and infant skin gets milder steroids.
visuals.alt: Body heat map of steroid absorption by site

points: Ointment from a 5 mm nozzle, **crease to fingertip** ≈ **0.5 g**, covers **two adult palms**.
Face & neck 2.5 · arm 3 · hand 1 · leg 6 · foot 2 · front trunk 7 · back 7. Whole body ≈ 40 FTU (20 g).
Face 15–30 g · hands 15–30 g · arms 30–60 g · legs 100 g · trunk 100 g · groins 15–30 g (recheck BNF).
Repeats, amount used, sites, atrophy, other diagnoses, infection, emollient use.

visuals.caption: One fingertip unit: ointment squeezed from the last finger crease to the tip of an adult index finger, about 0.5 g. It covers the area of two adult palms with fingers together.
visuals.alt: Ointment along an index finger beside two palms

manage.lead: Right potency, right place, right amount, right duration: then step down.

points: State **name, potency, site, frequency, duration and FTUs**, not ‘as directed’.
Emollient first, wait 15–30 min (or keep the same order).
Mild for mild, moderate for moderate, potent for severe (NICE CG57); **no potent steroids on the face** without advice.
Once controlled, step down; for frequent relapse, **weekend therapy** twice weekly to flare sites.
**TCI** (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) for face, eyelids, flexures: no atrophy.
Vitamin D analogues in psoriasis.

limits.t: After long-term moderate–potent use, on stopping: **reduce gradually**, seek specialist advice.
Large amounts of potent steroid, children, occlusion.
Never supply potent steroids for lightening: illegal use causes atrophy, striae, Cushing’s.

items.t: Children needing **very potent** steroid, or potent on face / flexures: specialist advice.
Suspected **TSW**, steroid **contact allergy** (patch test), widespread atrophy or striae.
Adult eczema not controlled after 4 weeks of correct potent TCS + emollients.

pearls.t: Write the FTU count: ‘2.5 FTU to face once daily for 5 days, then stop’.
Eyelids: mild, few days; TCI if recurrent; think IOP with long-term use.
UK uses **4 classes** (BNF), not the US 7-class list.
Under-treatment from steroid phobia is commoner than harm.

quiz.q: How much is one FTU and what does it cover?
quiz.a: About 0.5 g; two adult palms (~2% BSA).

quiz.q: Rash spreading on a steroid with scale at the edge?
What does MHRA advise after long-term potent use?
quiz.a: Reduce gradually, not abruptly; seek specialist advice if TSW suspected.
